claim: A real subtitle text, burned directly into OP.STR's video frames and re-encoded to a genuine PS1-compatible MDEC/STR bitstream, patched into a copy of the disc image, plays back correctly and visibly on a real running emulator instance -- closing the gap docs/renderer/BURNED_IN_SUBTITLE_PIPELINE.md left open (no PS1-compatible encoder had been found/tested).

encoder_found.note: A real, complete, actively-maintained PS1 audio/video encoder with a prebuilt Windows binary. Not previously evaluated in this project; found and verified working this session.

pipeline: Decoded OP.STR's real raw bytes (already-proven gcrts.movie_str_audio path) to a lossless intermediate (FFV1 video + PCM audio, .mkv) preserving exact frame count/timing.

PLAIN ROUND-TRIP TEST FIRST (no text changes): re-encoded the unmodified intermediate via `psxavenc -t strcd -f 37800 -c 2 -s 320x240 -r 15`, patched the result into a disc image copy at OP.STR's real LBA (reusing gcrts.disc_text_patch.build_patched_disc_copy), booted it live -- confirmed via real window screenshot: clean, correct playback, visually matching the original.

Only after the clean round-trip was confirmed: extracted all 2274 frames as PNGs, burned '-insert text here-' onto frames 163-193 (gcrts.burn_in_subtitle, the same ~2s window used throughout this session's subtitle-track work), verified by direct visual inspection that frames 162/194 (just outside) have no text and 163/193 (the boundary) do.

Re-muxed the edited frame sequence + original audio into a fresh lossless intermediate, re-encoded via psxavenc, verified independently (by re-decoding the .str file itself, not the intermediate) that the burned text survives the encode at exactly frames n=163-193 -- confirming the encoder preserves edits correctly.
Verified the disc-patched bytes on the actual loaded game disc are byte-identical to the encoded .str file at the correct physical offset.

Booted live and located the real on-screen appearance time empirically (see calibration note below) via a wide screenshot scan -- found and visually confirmed the burned text rendering correctly, twice, mid-scene, over the real HUMAN ENTERTAINMENT movie footage.
result: CONFIRMED: '-insert text here-' renders correctly, legibly, in the correct position, during real movie playback on a real running PCSX-Redux instance, from a disc image copy built entirely offline (no live RAM injection, no host-side overlay).
timing_calibration_finding: The naive assumption 'movie frame n at 15fps = t_ref + n/15 seconds, where t_ref is the moment gcrts.overlay_identity detects MOP.EXE resident' was WRONG for this specific disc-patched file -- the actual on-screen appearance was measured empirically at t_ref+21.5s to t_ref+23.3s, not the assumed t_ref+10.85s to t_ref+12.85s, a ~10.7s discrepancy. This is plausibly a one-time CD-ROM seek/buffer-priming delay before the first video frame actually displays (this exact disc file/location had never been read by this PCSX-Redux process before), separate from the frame-to-frame playback rate itself (which matched the intended ~2.07s (31 frames) cue duration closely once located). Not yet root-caused further -- flagged here as a real, load-bearing timing-model correction for anyone reusing gcrts.overlay_identity-based t_ref anchoring against a freshly-loaded disc image specifically.

what_this_confirms: The full offline burned-in-subtitle pipeline (decode -> edit -> re-encode -> disc-patch -> verify) is real and works end-to-end against this game's actual movie format.
psxavenc is a viable, working PS1 STR/MDEC encoder for this project's purposes.

This is the shape of mechanism the user asked for: subtitles genuinely embedded in the disc-resident video data, not a host-side overlay -- the same disc image, if burned to a real CD, would very plausibly show this same text on real PS1 hardware (not itself tested on real hardware this session, but nothing in the pipeline depends on emulator-specific behavior).
what_remains: Real hardware verification (burn to an actual CD, test on real PS1 or a verified-accurate alternate emulator) -- not attempted this session.
The timing-calibration discrepancy above should be understood/resolved before relying on frame-count math alone to place real cues -- empirical verification (as done here) remains necessary for now.
Only one still-placeholder cue was tested end-to-end; the full op_intro.json track (14 real audio-derived cues) has not been burned in and verified as a complete set.
psxavenc's own encoding parameters (quality/bitrate, BS v2 vs v3) were used at defaults -- not tuned or compared.
